item.title: Officers locate young gazelle held illegally in A-Ram
item.description:
Detectives from the Border Police Coastal District Central Unit, Border Police officers in Judea and Samaria, and Israel Nature and Parks Authority inspectors located a young Israeli gazelle overnight in the village of A-Ram. The gazelle is a protected wild animal that may not legally be hunted or kept in captivity.
The animal was transferred for further treatment to the wildlife hospital at the Ramat Gan Safari.
A 48-year-old resident of Kafr Aqab was detained for questioning on suspicion of illegally trading in, possessing, and hunting a protected natural asset.

item.title: Two arrested for attempting to carve opening in security barrier near Jerusalem
item.description:
Border Police officers arrested two residents of Kafr Aqab on suspicion of attempting to carve an opening at the base of the security barrier using electric power tools, with the aim of creating a passage from Judea and Samaria into Israel.
According to police, the two attempted to flee but were located after a brief chase inside a nearby residential building. A large drill and electrical cables allegedly used by the suspects were seized at the scene.

item.title: Ben-Gvir: Two of three killed in Silwan clashes threw stones, firebombs and were shot by police
item.description:
National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir claimed that two of the three people reported killed overnight during criminal clashes in Jerusalem's Silwan neighborhood had thrown stones and firebombs and were shot by police during the incident.
He said that portraying them as “murder victims" amounts to “social engineering."
